safety.title: Safety & Scrap Handling Guidelines
safety.subtitle: Essential protocols for households and scrap collectors to ensure safe recycling, hygiene, and emergency protection.
safety.householdItem1Desc: Keep paper, plastic, metal, and glass in separate dry bins. Clean food residue from containers to prevent contamination and odor.
safety.householdItem2Desc: Do not throw electronic scrap or lithium batteries into regular trash. Tape battery terminals and keep electronic scrap dry in a cool place.
safety.householdItem3Desc: Wrap broken glass, metal edges, and sharp objects securely in thick cardboard or newspaper before handoff to prevent injury to scrap collectors.
safety.collectorItem1Desc: Always wear cut-resistant gloves, heavy-duty closed footwear, and high-visibility vests during doorstep verification and transport.
safety.collectorItem2Desc: Lift heavy scrap bags using legs, not back. Seek assistance for scrap bundles exceeding 25kg or use hand trolleys.
safety.collectorItem3Desc: Refuse to collect medical waste, chemical containers, pressurized cylinders, or unidentified liquid drums. Report unsafe items immediately.
safety.emergencyDesc: In case of chemical exposure, severe cuts, or physical hazard during pickup, stop work immediately and contact local emergency services or the ScrapMax Support Helpline at 1800-123-SCRAP.
